{"id": "2:282/q81", "question": "What do the cited works report about Quranic collection and readings generally?", "turns_on": "The notes offer different readings, referents, grounds, or applications.", "positions": [{"id": "2:282/q81/p1", "position": "ALUSI-FULL supplies sciences context (v1p21 #2).", "reasons": "ALUSI-FULL (author): A good-chain Ibn Abi Dawud report from Abd Khayr says Ali called Abu Bakr the person with the greatest merit in the codices and the first to collect God's Book in the stated official sense. GHARNATI (author): The author says the Prophet had countless miracles besides the Qurʾan, but the Qurʾan is the clearest, wisest, most guiding, and most enduring miracle. GHARNATI (author): The Qurʾan joins proof and testimony with clarification of the path and the condition of each group, and remains directly observable to those who reflect. GHARNATI (author): Unlike other miracles known through later reports rather than direct observation, the Qurʾan remains pure and present for reflection across the ages."}, {"id": "2:282/q82/p2", "position": "BAQILLANI supplies rhetoric context (v1p284).", "reasons": "BAQILLANI (author): Punning can be learned from books such as Kitab al-Ajnas and Kitab al-ʿAyn, and antithesis is easier; the eloquence at issue in Qur’anic inimitability cannot be acquired by study. BAQILLANI (author): Learnable capacities converge at a customary limit, like human strength; exceeding that limit breaks convention and can serve as a prophetic sign under the proper conditions. BAQILLANI (author): Exceptional lines or phrases may occur rarely in a poet’s or writer’s work, so a person may be famed for only one or two; if all speech sustained that level, it could be called miraculous. BAQILLANI (author): Humans can produce a fine word or phrase, but cannot compose a surah or equivalent or attain the Qur’an’s level of eloquence and oratory. BAQILLANI (author): Eloquence means conveying the self’s intended meaning with the best sense and strongest wording, reaching the utterance’s full purpose."}, {"id": "2:282/q82/p3", "position": "BAQILLANI supplies rhetoric context (v1p286).", "reasons": "BAQILLANI (author): Speech becomes miraculous when it surpasses eloquence’s customary limit and reaches a level even the most accomplished practitioners cannot attain.
